cards.b: The actual place where a settlement is built (e.g. a river bend or hill-top).
Buildings clustered tightly around a central point such as a crossroads, well or church.
Buildings arranged in a line along a road, river, canal or coast.
Buildings widely scattered, such as isolated farms in upland areas.
Wet-point: near water supply. Dry-point: on dry ground, avoiding flooding.
Ranking of settlements by size and services: hamlet, village, town, city.
The area around a settlement from which people use its services. Larger for higher-order settlements.
The minimum number of customers needed to support a service.
Low-order: bought often and nearby (bread). High-order: bought rarely, travel further (cars, jewellery).
Highest land values, tall buildings, shops and offices, very accessible, congested, few residents.
Zone next to the CBD: old terraced housing and old factories, high density, often regenerated.
City edge with new estates, retail parks, golf courses and farmland; lowest land values.
An increase in the proportion of people living in towns and cities.
Rural-urban migration (push and pull factors) and natural increase of young migrants.
Residents get materials and services to build or improve their own homes.

gaps.s: A settlement built on dry ground to avoid flooding has a ___ site.
Buildings arranged in a line along a road are a ___ settlement.
The minimum number of customers needed to support a service is the ___ population.
The commercial centre of a city is called the ___.
The area from which people use a settlement's services is its sphere of ___.
Movement of people from cities back to the countryside is called ___.
Squatter settlements in Rio de Janeiro are known as ___.
Housing built without legal permission on land the residents do not own is called an ___ settlement.

short.q: Explain why the CBD has high land values.
short.model: It is the most accessible part of the city, where transport routes meet. Businesses compete for limited space to reach the most customers, which pushes prices up.

short.q: Explain why there are fewer cities than villages.
short.model: Cities need a large threshold population to support their many high-order services, so only a few places can grow that big. Villages need fewer customers.

short.q: Explain two causes of rapid urban growth in LICs.
short.model: Rural-urban migration happens because farm incomes are low and cities offer jobs and schools. Migrants are mainly young, so births are high and natural increase adds to growth.

short.q: Explain why informal settlements often have health problems.
short.model: They often lack clean water and sewers, so diseases such as cholera spread easily. Overcrowding and poor materials make this worse.

short.q: Explain how public transport can reduce congestion in a city.
short.model: Metros and buses carry many people at once, so fewer cars are needed on the road. This cuts traffic jams and air pollution.
